2. Tetragonal: a = b ≠ c, α = β = γ = 90°
3. Orthorhombic: a ≠ b ≠ c, α = β = γ = 90°
4. Monoclinic: a ≠ b ≠ c, α = γ = 90°, β ≠ 90°
5. Rhombohedral: a = b = c, α = β = γ ≠ 90°
6. Hexagonal: a = b ≠ c, α = β = 90°, γ = 120°

Now I'll examine each option:

A. Cubic and Rhombohedral: Both have a = b = c, but cubic has all angles at 90° while rhombohedral has all angles equal but not 90°. So they share the same unit cell dimensions but differ in axial angles.

B. Hexagonal and Cubic: Hexagonal has a = b ≠ c while cubic has a = b = c, so they don't share the same unit cell dimensions.

C. Monoclinic and Tetragonal: Monoclinic has a ≠ b ≠ c while tetragonal has a = b ≠ c, so they don't share the same unit cell dimensions.

D. Rhombohedral and Hexagonal: Rhombohedral has a = b = c while hexagonal has a = b ≠ c, so they don't share the same unit cell dimensions.

E. Tetragonal and Orthorhombic: Tetragonal has a = b ≠ c while orthorhombic has a ≠ b ≠ c, so they don't share the same unit cell dimensions.

Based on this analysis, only option A (Cubic and Rhombohedral) describes a pair of crystal systems that share the same type of unit cell dimensions (a = b = c) but differ in their axial angles.
